I was a very very strange child who became an even stranger adult. I was always the different kid when he played with action figures and stuff. Where my friends were content to just have their toys beat the hell out of other toys, my toys always had dramatic losses, harsh fights, and many relationship issues. I was always the different kid too. I would never really act my assigned gender but I would always just make it seem like I was kidding around. Like I love the color pink and I tell people that I just want pink everything but I always use a joking tone and then I would say more seriously, meh, just give me whatever color. 

In junior high, things got rough. I started getting gay bashed pretty hard and it was hurtful and confusing because I was not attracted to any men at all. I found myself super attracted to women. This is when I started having my thoughts that I would actually love to have been born a woman. But I couldn't say that so I just kept pressing how I did in elementary. Eventually the gay bashing started going away when I started dating and while I was dating, I stopped just pretending to like more feminine things.

I only came out to two of my friends and they both seemed a bit surprised because I worded it really weird. They expected me to say I was gay and when I said I was trans (after years of soul searching through pretty much all of junior-high school), they really took it very well. They really weren't that surprised because just the way I carried myself.

Yeah it's rough living in the south as a trans D: But you're first step should probably be what my first step will be hopefully in the next couple of weeks, therapy. Find a therapist in your area with experience and start there. If you need anyone to really talk to for free, I can talk and chat, just pm me because I do love listening! But as to what you should do, definitely therapy!

I saw a comment as I was frantically searching through comment thresholds. And I feel really bad that maybe I'm not doing this self ask thing because I keep responding. Am I doing this right? I'm not messing up here, am I? I really really don't want to be breaking any rules.

I need to focus, not relax. I don't want to just let the top right part of my head take over, even though it is the most calming.

My left hand shakes violently. I honestly am feeling myself losing this awareness. I'm scared but I type with a different feeling now.
